A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work, including Appendices A–H. Their text, equations, figures and tables support reliable comparison. The shorter checklist pagination in v4 does not omit content.

before.justification: Section 4.2 and Appendix G report original DP-SGD experiments on SST-2 and CIFAR-10, alongside numerical privacy-risk analyses and simulations.

after.justification: v4 retains the original SST-2 and CIFAR-10 experiments, numerical bound comparisons, Census risk analyses and statistical-query simulations.

M1.justification: The unified risk bounds, their use for noise calibration, and the evaluated training procedures remain unchanged. The revision repairs a mathematical proof without changing the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same Gaussian/Laplace mechanisms, binary attribute-inference scenarios, SST-2 and CIFAR-10 tasks, Census release and statistical-query scenarios. No coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain Cohen and Nissim’s PSO bound, Balle et al.’s RDP/zCDP bounds, Guo et al.’s Fano-based variants, and standard query-composition accounting. Comparator membership is unchanged.

E3.justification: The reported metrics, splits, mechanism parameters, noise sweeps and training settings are unchanged. Appendix G retains three epochs and batch size 256 for SST-2, and up to 100 epochs and batch size 8192 for CIFAR-10.

E4.justification: The Bernoulli-prior comparison in Appendix D, case studies in Appendix G, Census baseline analysis in Figure 9 and alternative PSO-bound analysis in Figure 10 are retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Appendix D retains ten repetitions for the Monte Carlo comparison and the same explanation that its error bars are not visible in Figure 5. No seed information, uncertainty-reporting practice or statistical test is added or revised.

E6.justification: Figures 1–10 and their associated passages retain the same values and findings. Both versions report the same within-paper accuracy comparisons: 52% versus 70% on SST-2 at risk 0.15, and 65% versus 68% on CIFAR-10 at risk 0.25.

T1.justification: Appendix C.1 corrects Lemma 2.1’s proof, which in v3 incorrectly equated randomized-test expectations with event probabilities. v4 uses a deterministic indicator for the forward implication and a Neyman–Pearson decomposition, including randomization when Λ(θ)=t, plus convexity for the reverse implication. This is a localized proof repair; the lemma and main bounds are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about unified and tunable privacy-risk bounds, tighter estimates, noise-calibration benefits, and generalization/memorization contributions. Their scientific scope is unchanged.

C2.justification: Sections 3.4 and 6 retain the same interpretations and qualifications concerning tightness, adversarial assumptions, privacy units and baseline gaming. The appendix discussions introduce no new applicability boundary or limitation.

D1.justification: Appendix G retains the same hyperparameter tables, hardware and runtime disclosures, and software list. The riskcal code-release information also remains unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 5, Appendix B and the bibliography retain the same cited works and research positioning. The added acknowledgment credits identification of the proof gap without introducing another cited research contribution.

P1.justification: Local edits rewrite the corrected proof’s prose, clarify the existing trade-off-function terminology, adjust appendix cross-reference wording, correct typographical details and add an acknowledgment. The overall section organization and narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v4 revises the proof’s equation displays and introduces limited reflow in the appendices and references, with tighter checklist spacing. All ten figures and the tables retain their content and structure.

improvement.justification: v4 repairs a genuine randomized-test gap in Appendix C.1’s proof of Lemma 2.1, including the previously omitted likelihood-ratio tie case. This strengthens the mathematical support for the unified bounds. The improvement is focused: the bounds, empirical evidence, main claims and limitations otherwise remain unchanged.
